summary: Go CronCreate has the same top-level tool name and basic inputs, stores session and durable jobs, and current cron-focused tests pass. The remaining parity gaps are in the exact tool result/error contract, durable feature-gating semantics, mixed-store max-job enforcement, durable-state robustness, and the scheduler lifecycle that CronCreate enables after creation.

gaps.title: CronCreate result and validation-error contract is text-only in Go
gaps.description: The TS tool has an output schema with id, humanSchedule, recurring, and durable, returns structured data from call(), and maps that data to the exact user-facing tool_result text. Its validation path also assigns errorCode 1-4 for invalid syntax, no future calendar match, max jobs, and teammate durable refusal. Go returns a single formatted Content string and IsError flag; only the teammate guard includes errorCode=4 text, while other validation failures are unstructured text.
gaps.impact: Consumers that expect TS-style structured CronCreate output or stable validation codes cannot reliably parse Go CronCreate results, and user-visible wording diverges from the original create result messages.

gaps.title: Durable cron kill switch is not modeled as effectiveDurable in Go
gaps.description: TS has a narrow durable-only gate, isDurableCronEnabled(), and CronCreate coerces durable=true to effectiveDurable=false when that gate is off while leaving session-only cron available. The prompt/description also changes when durable cron is disabled. Go has AGENT_TRIGGERS registration and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON full-tool refusal, but no durable-only resolver; durable input is passed directly into Store.create and reported directly in output.
gaps.impact: A durable feature rollback in TS becomes session-only creation, but Go would still persist durable jobs unless the entire cron feature is disabled. The model-facing description can also advertise durable behavior when a TS-equivalent durable kill switch should hide it.

gaps.title: Session-only creation does not enforce the global 50-job cap across durable jobs
gaps.description: TS validates MAX_JOBS against listAllCronTasks(), which merges durable file-backed tasks and session-only tasks. Go durable creation checks len(durable)+sessionCount, but the non-durable branch only checks len(sessionJobs), so creating session jobs can exceed 50 total jobs when durable jobs already exist.
gaps.impact: Go can admit more scheduled jobs than the TS limit in mixed durable/session use, increasing scheduler load and diverging from the original max-job error behavior.

gaps.title: Durable state reader is less tolerant of malformed files and malformed entries
gaps.description: TS readCronTasks returns an empty list for missing, inaccessible, empty, or malformed scheduled_tasks.json and skips individual malformed or invalid-cron entries. Go readDurableJobsLocked returns errors for JSON unmarshal failures and accepts zero-value fields such as empty id/prompt or CreatedAt=0 as long as cron parses. Durable CronCreate fails if the existing file is malformed because Store.create propagates the read error.
gaps.impact: A hand-edited or partially-written cron file can block durable CronCreate in Go where TS would recover by dropping bad state. Go can also keep malformed entries that TS would ignore, affecting max-job counts, listing, and firing.

gaps.title: Scheduler firing logic does not use the TS next-fire/jitter model that CronCreate promises
gaps.description: TS stores per-task nextFireAt, computes first sight from lastFiredAt ?? createdAt for recurring jobs and createdAt for one-shots, applies deterministic recurring and one-shot jitter, and then fires when now >= next. Go computes jitter for create/list output, but collectDueJobs fires by direct cron field match on the current minute. The Go scheduler therefore does not actually apply the jittered next_fire time it reports and does not use the same createdAt/lastFiredAt anchoring lifecycle.
gaps.impact: CronCreate output can claim a jittered next_fire that the Go scheduler will not honor. Recurring load spreading, one-shot early firing at :00/:30, restart reconstruction, and delayed-session behavior can all diverge from TS runtime behavior.

gaps.title: Startup missed-task lifecycle differs for one-shot and recurring jobs
gaps.description: TS initial load surfaces only missed one-shot tasks to the user, wraps the prompts in fenced text, prevents immediate raw firing, and removes them from scheduled_tasks.json. Recurring jobs are not surfaced as missed; they are handled by the normal check() path, which can fire and reschedule based on the anchored next-fire model. Go detectMissedRuns only scans recurring jobs with LastFiredAt and emits a missed-run notification; it does not handle missed one-shot durable tasks at startup and its normal scheduler only fires on exact current-minute cron matches.
gaps.impact: A durable one-shot that elapsed while Go was offline may remain scheduled instead of being surfaced and removed, while recurring missed runs are surfaced differently from TS. This changes user prompts, deletion lifecycle, and restart behavior for jobs created by CronCreate.

gaps.title: Runtime kill switch and idle/loading gate are not applied to actual firing
gaps.description: TS scheduler accepts isLoading and isKilled callbacks; every check skips firing while loading unless assistantMode and bails out when the cron gate is killed mid-session. Go checks CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON only when tools execute, not in runScheduler/collectDueJobs, and the IdleGate hook exists but is not called by StartCronPromptExecution or the scheduler.
gaps.impact: Existing Go jobs can continue firing after a TS-equivalent runtime kill switch flips, and they can fire while the runtime is busy/loading. The exported IdleGate gives a false sense of parity because it is not part of the firing path.

gaps.title: CronCreate does not accept TS semanticBoolean string inputs
gaps.description: TS preprocesses recurring and durable through semanticBoolean, accepting literal string inputs "true" and "false" while still advertising boolean schema. Go round-trips the input map through encoding/json into *bool and bool fields, so quoted booleans fail parsing before CronCreate can apply defaults or validation.
gaps.impact: Model-generated or client-generated CronCreate calls that TS accepts can fail in Go with invalid input, reducing robustness on optional boolean parameters.

candidate_tasks.title: Align CronCreate structured success and validation error contract
candidate_tasks.objective: Return CronCreate results and validation failures in a TS-compatible shape while preserving Go's existing human-readable content.
implementation_steps: Introduce a CronCreate result struct with id, humanSchedule, recurring, durable, and optional next_fire/tz metadata if the Go ToolResult type supports metadata; otherwise emit stable parseable content that exactly carries those fields.
Normalize successful user-facing text to distinguish recurring vs one-shot and durable vs session-only using TS wording.
Add stable error-code markers for invalid cron syntax, no future date, too many jobs, and durable teammate refusal.
Add tests for success fields and each validation code.
acceptance_criteria: CronCreate success exposes id, humanSchedule-equivalent schedule text, recurring, and effective durable status.
Invalid cron syntax maps to code 1, no future date to code 2, max jobs to code 3, and durable teammate refusal to code 4.
Existing basic CronCreate tests continue to pass.
risks: If types.ToolResult has no structured metadata field, exact TS data/result separation may require broader loop/types changes; keep this task scoped to CronCreate-visible contract unless that API already exists.
non_goals: Do not change CronDelete or CronList contracts except where shared helpers require it.

candidate_tasks.title: Add durable-only CronCreate kill switch and effectiveDurable semantics
candidate_tasks.objective: Match TS behavior where durable=true is coerced to session-only when the durable cron gate is disabled, without disabling session-only cron.
implementation_steps: Add a durable cron feature resolver or env-backed equivalent separate from CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON.
Compute effectiveDurable as requested durable && durable gate enabled before guardDurableCreation, Store.create, and output rendering.
Adjust CronCreate description/schema descriptions if the Go registry exposes dynamic descriptions; otherwise document the runtime behavior in tests.
Add tests proving durable=true becomes durable=false/session-only when the durable gate is off while normal cron remains enabled.
acceptance_criteria: A disabled durable gate does not reject CronCreate; it creates a session-only job.
The result reports durable=false when durable=true is coerced off.
CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON still disables the entire tool.
risks: Go may not have a GrowthBook equivalent; use an injectable resolver so production wiring can be added without hardcoding test-only env behavior.
non_goals: Do not implement a full GrowthBook client in this task unless one already exists in the Go codebase.

candidate_tasks.title: Enforce the global 50-job cap across session and durable CronCreate paths
candidate_tasks.objective: Ensure both durable and session-only creation count all scheduled jobs before admitting a new job.
implementation_steps: Add a helper that counts durable file-backed jobs plus session jobs under the appropriate locks.
Use that helper in both durable and non-durable Store.create branches.
Return the TS-compatible too-many-jobs message and error code from the CronCreate layer.
Add a mixed-store regression test with preseeded durable jobs followed by session-only creation.
acceptance_criteria: Creating a session-only job fails once durable + session jobs reaches 50.
Creating a durable job still fails at the same combined threshold.
The failure message remains 'Too many scheduled jobs (max 50). Cancel one first.' or the agreed TS-compatible equivalent.
risks: Care is needed to avoid lock-order deadlocks between the in-memory mutex and runtime file lock.
non_goals: Do not change the MAX_JOBS value.

candidate_tasks.title: Harden durable scheduled_tasks.json read compatibility
candidate_tasks.objective: Make Go durable cron state loading tolerate missing, unreadable, malformed, and partially malformed files the way TS readCronTasks does.
implementation_steps: Change readDurableJobsLocked to return an empty job list for malformed JSON and expected file-access failures that TS treats as inaccessible.
Validate each persisted entry has non-empty id, cron, prompt, and non-zero/valid createdAt before appending it.
Skip invalid cron entries instead of failing the whole file.
Add regression tests for malformed JSON, missing fields, invalid cron entries, and durable CronCreate after a bad file.
acceptance_criteria: A malformed scheduled_tasks.json does not block CronCreate durable creation.
Malformed individual entries are skipped and do not count toward the 50-job cap.
Valid entries in a mixed file still load and persist round-trip.
risks: Returning empty on malformed JSON can overwrite user-edited bad files on the next durable write, matching TS recovery but potentially discarding invalid content.
non_goals: Do not add migration support for alternate cron file paths.

candidate_tasks.title: Rework Go cron scheduler around TS next-fire, jitter, and anchoring semantics
candidate_tasks.objective: Ensure jobs created by CronCreate actually fire according to the same next-fire and deterministic jitter model reported to the user.
implementation_steps: Introduce per-job nextFireAt state for session and durable jobs.
Compute first-sight next fire from lastFiredAt ?? createdAt for recurring jobs and from createdAt for one-shot jobs.
Apply recurring jitter based on the interval between cron matches, not a fixed one-minute proxy.
Apply one-shot early jitter and clamp to createdAt/from time.
Persist LastFiredAt for durable recurring jobs after firing so restarts reconstruct the same next fire.
Update create/list next_fire computation to use the same helper as the scheduler.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler fires at the jittered next fire, not merely on raw cron minute match.
Create output next_fire matches the scheduler's first fire time within test-controlled clock precision.
Recurring durable jobs persist LastFiredAt and do not refire immediately after store rebuild unless due under TS semantics.
One-shot jobs at :00/:30 can fire early according to deterministic jitter.
risks: This changes core firing timing and must use deterministic clocks in tests to avoid flakes.
It may require replacing current direct cron match logic rather than patching around it.
non_goals: Do not change CronDelete/List public behavior except next_fire consistency.

candidate_tasks.title: Match TS startup missed-task lifecycle
candidate_tasks.objective: Handle missed durable one-shot and recurring tasks on startup with the same notification, removal, and rescheduling semantics as TS.
implementation_steps: Replace or extend detectMissedRuns so initial load identifies missed one-shot durable tasks using nextCronRun(createdAt) < now.
Surface missed one-shot tasks using fenced prompt text that tells the model to ask before executing.
Remove surfaced one-shot missed tasks from scheduled_tasks.json.
Do not surface recurring tasks as missed notifications; let the next-fire scheduler path fire/reschedule them according to TS semantics.
Add tests for missed one-shot removal and recurring non-notification on initial load.
acceptance_criteria: A missed one-shot durable task is surfaced once, fenced safely, and removed from the cron file.
Recurring missed tasks are not surfaced through the one-shot missed notification path.
No raw missed one-shot prompt fires before user confirmation.
risks: Existing Go tests currently assert recurring missed-run notification behavior; those tests must be intentionally updated to the TS contract.
non_goals: Do not implement AskUserQuestion execution; only produce the scheduler notification prompt equivalent.

candidate_tasks.title: Wire firing-time idle/loading gate and runtime cron kill switch
candidate_tasks.objective: Make the actual Go firing path honor the same mid-session skip conditions that TS applies before any cron side effects.
implementation_steps: Add injectable isKilled and isLoading/idle policy callbacks to CronStore or the scheduler loop.
Check the kill switch before collecting or firing due jobs.
Call IdleGateConsult or a runtime-provided loading policy before callback execution; skip/defer firing when the policy says not to fire.
Wire registry defaults so behavior is no-op when no richer runtime policy is available.
Add tests proving a disabled runtime gate and a false IdleGate prevent callback execution.
acceptance_criteria: Existing scheduled jobs stop firing when the runtime cron kill switch is enabled.
IdleGate=false prevents StartCronPromptExecution or scheduler callback from launching a background agent.
Default behavior remains fire-allowed when no policy is configured.
risks: Skipping versus deferring must be chosen to match TS: TS check simply returns and retries next tick while the task remains scheduled.
non_goals: Do not implement OS-level idle/battery detection in this task.

candidate_tasks.title: Accept TS semanticBoolean values for CronCreate optional booleans
candidate_tasks.objective: Allow CronCreate recurring and durable to accept literal string booleans exactly as TS semanticBoolean does.
implementation_steps: Add a small semantic boolean decoder for CronCreateInput that accepts bool, "true", and "false" without treating arbitrary non-empty strings as true.
Preserve current defaults: recurring omitted means true, durable omitted means false.
Reject other string values with a clear invalid-input ToolResult.
Add tests for recurring="false", recurring="true", durable="true", durable="false", and invalid durable="yes please".
acceptance_criteria: CronCreate accepts quoted "true" and "false" for recurring and durable.
CronCreate does not accept truthy arbitrary strings.
Other tools are unaffected unless a reusable helper is deliberately adopted with tests.
risks: A generic parser change could affect unrelated tools; keep decoding local to CronCreate unless broader parity work requests it.
non_goals: Do not change the advertised JSON schema type from boolean.
